scenes.line1: How sure are you about your estimate?
scenes.line2: What does a confidence interval show?
scenes.say: How sure are you about your estimate? What does a confidence interval actually show?

scenes.label: Interval
scenes.sub: A confidence interval gives a range where a population value likely falls, based on your sample.
scenes.say: A confidence interval gives you a range where the real population value probably sits, based on your sample.

rows.b: Standard deviation divided by root of sample size

scenes.say: You build a confidence interval using your sample mean, the standard error—which is the standard deviation divided by the square root of your sample size—and a z-score for your confidence level.

For a ninety-five percent confidence interval, use your mean plus or minus one point nine six times the standard deviation over root n. This assumes a normal distribution and you know the population standard deviation.

scenes.question: Does 95% CI mean 95% chance true value is inside?
scenes.wrong: Yes, the true value has a 95% chance.
scenes.right: No—over many samples, 95% of intervals will contain the true value. The true value is fixed; the interval is random.
scenes.say: Careful: a ninety-five percent confidence interval doesn't mean there's a ninety-five percent chance the true value is inside. It means if you repeated the experiment many times, ninety-five percent of those intervals would capture the true value.
